title: CTET Exam Guide: Central Teacher Eligibility Test Paper 1 & 2 Roadmap
summary: Complete preparation guide for CBSE CTET Paper 1 (Primary) and Paper 2 (Upper Primary) to qualify for KVS, NVS, DSSSB, and central school teaching jobs.
author: Sarkari Aavedan Editorial Team
content:
## Introduction

The Central Teacher Eligibility Test (CTET), conducted bi-annually by the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE), is the mandatory eligibility benchmark for appointment as a teacher in central schools (Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan - KVS, Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti - NVS, Central Tibetan Schools, and Army Public Schools) as well as Union Territory schools (DSSSB, Chandigarh, Ladakh). CTET certificate validity is now **lifetime**, making it a permanent asset for all teaching aspirants.

## Eligibility Criteria

| Paper | Teaching Level | Required Educational Qualifications |
|---|---|---|
| **CTET Paper-I** | Primary Stage (Classes I to V) | Senior Secondary (10+2) with at least 50% marks AND 2-year Diploma in Elementary Education (D.El.Ed) OR 4-year Bachelor of Elementary Education (B.El.Ed) OR 2-year Diploma in Education (Special Education). Candidates appearing in final year can apply. |
| **CTET Paper-II** | Elementary Stage (Classes VI to VIII) | Graduation AND 2-year Diploma in Elementary Education OR Graduation with at least 50% marks AND 1-year/2-year Bachelor in Education (B.Ed) OR 4-year B.El.Ed / B.A/B.Sc.Ed / B.A.Ed/B.Sc.Ed. Candidates in final year can apply. |

## Age Limit & Qualifying Standards

| Parameter | Specifications |
|---|---|
| **Minimum Age** | 18 Years (No upper age limit for CTET eligibility) |
| **General (UR) Cut-off** | 60% (90 Marks out of 150 Marks) to qualify |
| **OBC / SC / ST / PwBD Cut-off** | 55% (82 Marks out of 150 Marks) to qualify |
| **Negative Marking** | **No Negative Marking** (1 mark awarded for every correct answer) |
| **Validity of Certificate** | Lifetime validity across all states and central schools |

## Examination Structure & Pattern

### Paper I (For Primary Teachers - Classes I to V)
| Subject | Questions | Maximum Marks | Time Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Child Development and Pedagogy (CDP)** | 30 Questions | 30 Marks | Combined 150 Minutes (2.5 Hours) |
| **Language I (Compulsory - Choice from 20 languages)** | 30 Questions | 30 Marks | Combined |
| **Language II (Compulsory - Different from Language I)** | 30 Questions | 30 Marks | Combined |
| **Mathematics (Content + Pedagogy)** | 30 Questions | 30 Marks | Combined |
| **Environmental Studies (EVS) (Content + Pedagogy)** | 30 Questions | 30 Marks | Combined |
| **Grand Total** | **150 Questions** | **150 Marks** | **150 Minutes** |

### Paper II (For Elementary Teachers - Classes VI to VIII)
| Subject | Questions | Maximum Marks | Time Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Child Development and Pedagogy (CDP)** | 30 Questions | 30 Marks | Combined 150 Minutes (2.5 Hours) |
| **Language I (Compulsory)** | 30 Questions | 30 Marks | Combined |
| **Language II (Compulsory)** | 30 Questions | 30 Marks | Combined |
| **Mathematics and Science** (For Maths/Science teachers) OR **Social Studies/Social Science** (For Social Studies teachers) | 60 Questions | 60 Marks | Combined (40 content + 20 pedagogy) |
| **Grand Total** | **150 Questions** | **150 Marks** | **150 Minutes** |

## Proven Preparation Strategy

| Phase | Targeted Action Plan |
|---|---|
| **Phase 1: Master Child Development & Pedagogy (CDP)** | Study major theories of child development: Jean Piaget (Cognitive Development), Lev Vygotsky (Sociocultural Theory), Lawrence Kohlberg (Moral Development), and Inclusive Education. CDP carries 30 direct marks and 15 marks within each subject pedagogy (total 90+ marks across the paper). |
| **Phase 2: NCERT Content Mastery (Classes 3 to 8)** | For Paper-I, read NCERT EVS and Maths textbooks of Classes 3, 4, and 5 thoroughly. For Paper-II, study NCERT Science, Mathematics, or History/Polity/Geography textbooks of Classes 6, 7, and 8 line by line. |
| **Phase 3: Language Passages & Grammar** | Practice unseen prose and poetry passages. In CTET, language questions are passage-based rather than rote grammar rules. Master teaching of language skills (LSRW: Listening, Speaking, Reading, Writing). |
| **Phase 4: Solve 10 Previous Year Question Papers (PYQs)** | CBSE repeats pedagogical concepts and question patterns extensively. Solve papers from 2018 to 2026 under exam timing to comfortably score 110+ marks. |

Qualifying CTET opens up prestigious recruitment avenues with regular central pay scales in KVS, NVS, and DSSSB. Focus heavily on pedagogical understanding to clear the exam in your very first attempt.
